principles: References are quality standards, never scene templates.
Typography is primary; support visuals strengthen meaning.
One dominant visual/motion event at a time unless deliberate contrast requires two.
Continuity carriers are preferred over full reset when adjacent beats share evidence.
Native 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9 compositions are semantic siblings, not crops.
Motion reinforces reading order and semantic change.
Technical pass cannot overrule weak visual judgment.

patterns.semantic_use: Hook, promise, setup, or cumulative claim where meaning becomes stronger as phrase completes
typography_behavior: Reveal semantic chunks, not arbitrary word-by-word typing
Preserve semantic line breaks
Allow final keyword/phrase to promote in scale/weight
support_visual_behavior: Support visual may already be present at low dominance
Do not add a second dominant event while hero builds

motion_behavior.exit: may collapse/reconfigure into next evidence scene

native_aspect_adaptations.9x16: stack vertically; 2–4 semantic lines; support object below/behind with generous white space
native_aspect_adaptations.1x1: compact 2–3 line lockup; support object may sit offset lower-right/left
native_aspect_adaptations.16x9: use lateral negative space; text can build left while support visual occupies opposite field

misuse_conditions: Every beat; reserve for claims whose meaning benefits from accumulation

reference_evidence.observation: hero builds from setup to large payoff phrase while UI proof remains secondary
headline expands semantically while supporting human illustration stays stable

typography_behavior: Stage A must stop being readable before Stage B becomes dominant
Replacement may reuse position or deliberately reconfigure
Promote the changed concept rather than repeating full sentence
support_visual_behavior: Supporting visual may persist as continuity carrier if it remains semantically valid

native_aspect_adaptations.9x16: vertical replacement at same anchor or top-to-center reconfiguration
native_aspect_adaptations.16x9: can replace laterally or collapse split comparison into single statement

misuse_conditions: Changing support visual when persistence would aid continuity

reference_evidence.observation: setup copy gives way to large payoff word/phrase rather than coexisting
new semantic statement enters with changed human pose

patterns.semantic_use: Payoff word, critical number, product/name reveal, decisive contrast
typography_behavior: One word/short phrase grows to become clear visual center
Support copy becomes quieter
Scale contrast should carry meaning rather than decoration
support_visual_behavior: Supporting visual must retreat, crop, or remain subordinate

motion_behavior.entry: promoted unit emerges from existing text or clean cut

native_aspect_adaptations.9x16: large center/top-center vertical word with room for support below
native_aspect_adaptations.1x1: large central lockup with asymmetric support
native_aspect_adaptations.16x9: large lateral or centered word; use horizontal breathing room

reference_evidence.observation: strong scale contrast converts setup text into dominant payoff phrase

patterns.semantic_use: Move from claim to proof/demo without losing narrative continuity
typography_behavior: Hero resolves first; a keyword/label can remain as anchor
Support text introduces what the proof demonstrates
support_visual_behavior: Screenshot/app window/card enters only after claim is readable
Evidence becomes dominant visual after handoff

motion_behavior.exit: evidence may persist into next beat

native_aspect_adaptations.9x16: hero top; evidence card expands into lower 45–55%
native_aspect_adaptations.16x9: hero and evidence can trade left/right dominance

misuse_conditions: Evidence appearing before viewer understands claim

reference_evidence.observation: large hero resolves then scene switches to tiny setup + product window
headline and screenshot share hierarchy before evidence persists into next question

patterns.semantic_use: Adjacent beats discuss the same product/proof surface
typography_behavior: Headline/support copy may replace around a stable evidence object
support_visual_behavior: Keep screenshot/card on screen and reposition/resize rather than reintroducing from zero

motion_behavior.continuity: evidence object persists across beat boundary
motion_behavior.text: new claim replaces old around persistent anchor

native_aspect_adaptations.9x16: evidence can stay center/lower and text changes above
native_aspect_adaptations.1x1: evidence offset anchor may slide modestly
native_aspect_adaptations.16x9: evidence remains on one side while text region changes

reference_evidence.observation: same UI evidence persists while headline changes to new semantic question

patterns.semantic_use: Product proof, interface demonstration, code, document, repository, real evidence
typography_behavior: Headline should state takeaway, not describe every visible detail
Use short annotation/label if needed
support_visual_behavior: Frame/crop screenshot cleanly; mild shadow/depth allowed; preserve legibility
Use callout arrow/line only for exact evidence target

motion_behavior.exit: can become continuity carrier or collapse into label

native_aspect_adaptations.9x16: portrait crop or stacked window; avoid tiny full desktop
native_aspect_adaptations.1x1: crop to relevant region; one primary evidence surface
native_aspect_adaptations.16x9: can show wider UI with annotation zone

misuse_conditions: Using fake UI as proof when real supplied UI exists

reference_evidence.observation: large product/interface crops function as proof beneath concise headline
code window plus short bullets; evidence remains primary visual

patterns.semantic_use: Short proof points, requirements, features, constraints after a clear headline
typography_behavior: List items are subordinate to hero
Reveal each item in reading order
Keep line length short
support_visual_behavior: Optional small icon/check/cue per item only if it improves scanning

motion_behavior.sequence: items reveal with 2–5 frame stagger or short semantic holds
motion_behavior.exit: list can compress into one summary phrase

native_aspect_adaptations.16x9: list can sit beside evidence rather than under

reference_evidence.observation: ONE COMMAND headline + screenshot + progressively revealed no-setup/no-config list

patterns.semantic_use: Clarification, italic aside, explanatory tail after a strong claim
typography_behavior: Support enters later and quieter
Smaller scale, lighter weight or italic allowed
Never compete with hero
support_visual_behavior: Support visual should remain static/subtle during reading

motion_behavior.exit: may stay while next object transition begins

native_aspect_adaptations.9x16: place below hero with generous line-height

misuse_conditions: Using support to carry the main idea

reference_evidence.observation: large OpenCode carrier with quiet italic support copy building beneath

patterns.semantic_use: Two alternatives, before/after, manual/automatic, expensive/free, fragmented/shared
typography_behavior: Use spatial contrast first; collapse to winner/summary after comparison
Different text weights can signal hierarchy
support_visual_behavior: Use paired evidence/objects only when both sides are meaningful

motion_behavior.resolution: winning/reframed statement becomes single dominant lockup

misuse_conditions: Comparison where no real contrast exists

reference_evidence.observation: pricing/model comparisons use text and product surfaces with decisive hierarchy

patterns.semantic_use: A keyword should become, reveal, or attach to a concrete object/evidence surface

Text may shrink/move into label position
